newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE, FIRMER ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE, FIRMER ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer on Wednesday, dealers said.
"The market opened quite liquid but the Reserve Bank has taken off Z$300 million (by way of selling treasury bills) and its a bit tight now," commented one dealer.

He said discount houses had taken up the central bank paper at a 16.64 percent yield, up from Tuesday's 16.52 percent and were selling the bills on the secondary market at 16.35 percent from 16.25 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 17.25 and 17 percent respectively from 17 and 16.50 percent while bankers acceptances were steady at 16.75 percent (buying) and 16.50 percent (selling).
Call money was also unchanged at 16.25 percent in a market which opened in surplus of Z$142.6 million, up from Z$260 million.
